topic: How AirTags Find Things (B: story first)

lines.say: The airline told her the bag was safe. Her AirTag showed it at a random apartment complex.
lines.show: The *airline* told her the bag was *safe.* Her AirTag showed it at a [random apartment complex.]

lines.say: But the AirTag didn't find it. A stranger's phone did.
lines.show: But the AirTag *didn't* find it. A [stranger's phone] did.

lines.say: An AirTag has no GPS. No SIM. No Wi-Fi. It talks over Bluetooth, on a coin battery.
lines.show: An AirTag has *no GPS.* No SIM. No Wi-Fi. It talks over *Bluetooth,* on a [coin battery.]

lines.say: Over and over, it whispers one thing: I'm here.
lines.show: Over and over, it *whispers* one thing: [I'm here.]

lines.say: Any nearby iPhone hears it, even yours. It adds its own location, locks it, and sends it to Apple.
lines.show: Any nearby *iPhone* hears it, [even yours.] It adds its *own location,* locks it, and [sends it to Apple.]

lines.say: Then her phone downloads that report, unlocks it, and there's her bag.
lines.show: Then *her phone* downloads that report, unlocks it, and [there's her bag.]

lines.say: Only she holds the key. Apple can't read the location, and the stranger can't see whose tag it is.
lines.show: Only *she* holds the key. Apple [can't read] the location, and the stranger can't see *whose tag* it is.

lines.say: Now repeat that across hundreds of millions of Apple devices. That's how a twenty-nine dollar disc knew more than the airline.
lines.show: Now repeat that across *hundreds of millions* of Apple devices. That's how a *$29 disc* knew [more than the airline.]

lines.say: And to stop stalkers: if an unknown AirTag travels with you, your phone can warn you. iPhone or Android.
lines.show: And to stop *stalkers:* if an unknown AirTag *travels with you,* your phone can [warn you.] iPhone or Android.

lines.say: So that little disc doesn't know where it is. Everyone around it does.
lines.show: So that little disc *doesn't know where it is.* [Everyone around it does.]
